subject: Difference in submitting observation covariates as list or as df

messages.author: c2a477445d711b46
messages.subject: Difference in submitting observation covariates as list or as df
parts:
Hi there,

I noticed that it is possible to pass to the unmarkedFrame method a
"properly formatted" data frame. (I had a dataset that I thought was
ready for it). Notably, the resulting frame is different from that
when I pass the list, because I must be improperly formatting it (as
example below shows). Were I to format the data frame correctly, is
it still OK to use that with the method instead of a list?

Thanks for any help. It is not really a game stopper for me, but
maybe I will eventually run into a dataset that uses the proper
format.
Leo
Example code:
library(unmarked)
dd<-
data.frame(y1=c(0,1,2,1),y2=c(0,2,3,2),var1.1=c(4,5,6,7),var1.2=c(3,1,2,3),var2.1=c(3,4,3,2),var2.2=c(5,3,2,4))
ocdf1<-dd[,c("var1.1","var2.1")];names(ocdf1)<-c("var1","var2")
ocdf2<-dd[,c("var1.2","var2.2")];names(ocdf2)<-c("var1","var2")
ocdf<-rbind(ocdf1,ocdf2)
ocovs<-
list(var1=dd[,c("var1.1","var1.2")],var2=dd[,c("var2.1","var2.2")])
udf1<-unmarkedFramePCount(y=dd[,1:2],obsCovs=ocdf)
udf2<-unmarkedFramePCount(y=dd[,1:2],obsCovs=ocovs)
identical(udf1,udf2)
#visual inspection shows why
udf1@obsCovs;udf2@obsCovs

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Difference in submitting observation covariates as list or as df
parts:
Hi Leo,

Yes, you can format obsCovs as either a list or a data.frame. However, the data.frame option is a little confusing as you have found out because it must be in row-major order. This means that you need to transpose each matrix before converting it into a vector. Like this:

var1 <- cbind(ocdf1[,1], ocdf2[,1])
var2 <- cbind(ocdf1[,2], ocdf2[,2])
ocdf<-data.frame(var1=as.vector(t(var1)), var2=as.vector(t(var2)))
So, it's easier to just use a list. This is briefly documented on the unmarkedFrame help page.

Richard
